To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the crust‐ core boundary acts as a potential for the neutron vortices, (ii) the proton vortices are annihilated in a continuous manner at the crust‐ core surface during the interglitches, and (iii) the discontinuous annihilation of proton vortex clusters at the crust-core surface restores the neutron vortex flow through the interface and spins up the crust, resulting in a glitch.

the interaction between the crustal magnetic flux and the neutron vortex flux leads to the generation of a potential barrier for vortices at crust‐core interface, which causes the stopping of the neutron vortex current through this interface.

(1) vortex-interface interaction leads to the storage of angular momentum in the crustal layers during the interglitches, (2) the stored angular momentum is released in the form of glitches, and (3) the observed glitch characteristics, such as their size and recurrence time, can be understood in the light of the vortex-interface interaction

the following questions: (1) What are the properties of the neutron star crust and its interface with the core? (2) How do these properties affect the dynamics of the crust and core, and the interaction of the crust and the core superfluids?

the interface is a potential barrier to vortices and the crust is spun up by a discontinuous annihilation of vortices.
